- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model often overshoots early; cap forecast decline after 3–5 days of negative sentiment.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent mean) — apply smoothing filter to prevent 3–5 day overshoots.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to overforecast mid-range; adjust downward by 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 10–14 days after peak, model often fails to correct — apply decay factor (e.g., 0.95 per day) to forecast tail.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) — reduce first 5 days by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon.
